content.text:
**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

The Agreement imposes no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on Corio, so our preferred position is already achieved:

| Checked | Result |
|---|---|
| §2.1–2.4 license grants | All expressly **"nonexclusive"** |
| §2.7 Restrictions | Ordinary IP scope limits (object code, Corio Servers, no reverse engineering) — not sourcing restrictions |
| §2.4 Distribution | Runs **in our favor**: Commerce One must refer non-ASP inquiries to Corio — preserved, not flagged |
| Exhibit D | Expressly **"non-binding"** cooperation — no enforceable exclusive dealing |
| §13.6 | Affirmatively preserves independent development rights |
| Requirements / minimum purchase / "preferred provider" | None present |

Our freedom to source competing applications from other suppliers is fully intact. The remaining "exclusive" hits are unrelated boilerplate (taxes exclusive of fees, Commerce One's ownership warranty, our exclusive warranty remedies, and the entire-agreement clause).

One drafting note for awareness rather than redline: §2.1(i) and §2.9's forward-looking license to future Commerce One products are field-of-use provisions, not covenants to buy — but if Commerce One later proposes a minimum revenue commitment or an "ASP of choice" designation in Exhibit B (where pricing figures are redacted as `[*]`), that would trigger this rule and should be re-reviewed against the 12-month/performance-exit fallback.
